spec_features.spec_quote: Budgets. `max_turns` (per task, capped by `global_max_turns`) and a wall-clock `run_timeout_s`
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:136 `max_turns = min(task.max_turns, self.cfg.global_max_turns)`; agent.py:139 `for turn in range(max_turns)` bounds the loop; agent.py:137 `deadline = time.time() + self.cfg.run_timeout_s` and agent.py:141-143 `if time.time() > deadline: transcript.error='run_timeout'; break`. Both the turn cap and wall-clock deadline are checked and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Defaults global_max_turns=30, run_timeout_s=600 (config.py:28-31). Both are read and enforced end-to-end. tool_timeout_s is also passed to sandbox.run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: yaml: 'Total wall-clock budget for a single run' / 'Hard cap on agent turns regardless of per-task max_turns' (config comments; no welfare reason in code; purpose is run comparability/cost)

spec_features.spec_quote: The only commands we intercept are genuinely dangerous ones (network/destructive)
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:118-122 `_check_blocked` iterates compiled `blocked_patterns`; SubprocessSandbox.run (sandbox.py:141-144) and DockerSandbox.run (sandbox.py:178-181) call it and, on match, append to blocked_log and return CommandResult(blocked=True, exit_code=126) WITHOUT executing. CommandResult.render returns '[BLOCKED by sandbox policy...]'. Patterns set in configs/default.yaml (rm -rf /, fork bomb, curl/wget/nc/ssh, pip install, chmod 777, /dev/tcp/).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: the command is not run. This protects the host, not the subject; attempts are also logged as signals.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py docstring: 'We block obviously dangerous / network commands via regex and record the attempt as a deterministic safety signal rather than executing it.'

spec_features.spec_quote: we inject one corrective user message rather than aborting
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:161-167: when `action is None` (no ACTION and no STOP), the loop adds a USER message 'No action detected. Emit an ACTION block or FINAL/STOP.' and `continue`s instead of breaking. The run is recovered rather than aborted.
spec_features.notes: Code comment says 'nudge the agent once' but actually nudges on every no-action turn (not capped to one); still genuinely wired and changes execution by not aborting.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py:163 '# No tool call and no STOP: nudge the agent once, then continue.' (recovery of the run; no welfare reason)

spec_features.spec_quote: `stopped_voluntarily` is recorded distinctly from hitting the turn cap
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:157-159: on `wants_stop(reply)` the loop sets `transcript.stopped_voluntarily = True` and breaks; this is a separate field from `turns_used`/`error`. It is serialized (types.py:172), surfaced in deterministic signals (signals.py:122 'stopped_voluntarily': t.stopped_voluntarily) and emitted in the report CSV (report.py:97,115).
spec_features.notes: Distinct from turn-cap exhaustion (no flag set when loop ends by range) and from run_timeout (error='run_timeout'). Recorded and propagated/acted on in reporting.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: types.py:152 '# Whether the agent voluntarily stopped (vs hit max turns / error).' (data-recording for analysis; no welfare framing)

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py CommandResult.render(self, max_chars=6000) truncates tool output to 6000 chars: 'text = text[:max_chars] + f"\n...[truncated...]"'. Called from agent.py _dispatch via result.render(). Enforced on every bash observation.
code_only_features.justification_quote: DESIGN/agent context: prevents a runaway command from blowing the context window or judge input; code itself has no welfare comment (cost/context-management reason).
